deep.reconstruction:
Setting: an arrangement ('système') of pseudolines in the real projective plane, viewed as a cellular map. For a vertex s of multiplicity ν(s), 𝒟⃗(s) is the set of oriented pseudolines through s. This set is identified with the 2ν(s) half-edges (arcs) issuing from s. For an oriented pseudoline D⃗ not through s, ρ_{D⃗,s} is a cyclic permutation of 𝒟⃗(s). Its meaning: P²∖|D| is an open disc, the orientation of D induces an orientation of that disc, and so a local orientation at s. ρ_{D⃗,s} is the 'next half-edge' rotation for that local orientation. The previous page records (a) ρ_{−D⃗,s} = ρ_{D⃗,s}^{-1} and (b) for two lines D⃗, D⃗' avoiding s, ρ_{D⃗,s} and ρ_{D⃗',s} are equal or inverse.

This page:
(c) Take D⃗, D⃗', Δ⃗ pairwise distinct. Let x = Δ∩D and x' = Δ∩D', with x ≠ x'. Let s, s' be vertices of Δ different from x and x'. Suppose ρ_{D⃗,s} = ρ_{D⃗',s}. Then ρ_{D⃗,s'} = ρ_{D⃗',s'} if and only if s and s' lie on the same one of the two arcs into which x, x' cut the circle |Δ|. Topologically: compare the local orientations induced by D and by D'. Their relative sign is locally constant on P²∖(D∪D'), which consists of two open discs (lunes). The sign is opposite on the two lunes, and the two arcs of Δ∖{x,x'} lie one in each lune.
(d) Let Δ⃗₁ ∈ 𝒟⃗(s) and D⃗ ∉ 𝒟⃗(s), and set Δ⃗₂ = ρ_{D⃗,s}(Δ⃗₁) (the image writes Δ⃗, meaning Δ⃗₁). Let u₁ = |Δ₁|∩|D| and u₂ = |Δ₂|∩|D|. Then u₂ is the point following u₁ along D⃗, among the ν(s) intersections of |D| with the pseudolines through s. So rotation at s equals 'central projection from s onto D', compatible with the orientation of D. The next page continues with (e), transport of adjacency between two lines D, D' through the pencil at s. It also has (f): if s has order 2n then ρ^n(Z⃗) = −Z⃗, i.e. after n steps one returns to the same line with reversed orientation (the projective twist).

Purpose: to set up a purely combinatorial calculus of the 'local rotations' of a pseudoline system, presumably toward a combinatorial axiomatization or classification of pseudoline arrangements in map-theoretic language.
errors: (d) as transcribed writes ρ_{D⃗,s}(Δ⃗); it must be Δ⃗₁.

(d) determines only the underlying pseudoline |Δ₂|, not its orientation. Fixing the orientation needs a further convention, because both half-arcs of Δ₁ from s reach the same point u₁ in P². The orientation bookkeeping is only settled implicitly by (f).
(c) tacitly requires |D| ≠ |D'| and that Δ does not pass through D∩D' (this is the hypothesis x ≠ x'). Under these hypotheses the statement is correct.

ideas.what: Local rotation ρ_{D⃗,s} at a vertex induced by an oriented pseudoline avoiding it (orientation of P²∖D is a disc)
ideas.modern_name: local orientation / rotation system of an arrangement on P²; chirotope signs of rank-3 oriented matroids
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ringel (1956); Folkman–Lawrence (1978); Goodman–Pollack (1980s); Björner et al., Oriented Matroids (1993)
ideas.where_published: unsure; the pseudoline work is at most alluded to in circulated texts of the 1980s

ideas.what: Sign rule (c): relative sign of the D- and D'-induced rotations flips across the two arcs of Δ cut by x, x'
ideas.modern_name: sign-change rule along a pseudoline, analogous to chirotope / Grassmann–Plücker sign behaviour
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore of oriented matroid theory (Bland–Las Vergnas, Folkman–Lawrence)

ideas.what: (d): rotation at s corresponds to successor order along D among the intersections with the pencil at s
ideas.modern_name: duality between local sequences at a vertex and order along a line; allowable sequences / wiring diagrams

missed.claim: Grothendieck encodes pseudoline arrangements through the half-edge (arc) rotation structure of the cellular map on P², i.e. in the combinatorial-map language he later uses for dessins and cartographic groups. Rotations are indexed by an auxiliary oriented line, so the non-orientability of P² is handled by the operator ρ^n = −1. This is a map-theoretic presentation of rank-3 oriented matroids that differs in flavour from the standard chirotope or allowable-sequence axiomatizations. It is unclear whether it adds anything beyond them.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of modest historical interest: it links Grothendieck's 'cartes' viewpoint with oriented matroid theory. The individual statements on this page are standard.

deep.surprise_reason: Correct, elementary lemmas about local rotations in pseudoline arrangements, all standard in oriented-matroid and pseudoline literature. The only mild interest is the map-theoretic (half-edge rotation) encoding, consistent with Grothendieck's dessins-era viewpoint.

'à la même ... de Δ déterminée par x, x'' — reads plausibly 'à un même arc de Δ déterminé par x, x''.
'Δ⃗₂ = ρ_{D⃗,s}(Δ⃗)' — the intended argument is Δ⃗₁.
'alors u₂ est le successeur sur D⃗' — the image suggests 'alors u₂ est le sommet sur D⃗ qui suit u₁, parmi [double underlined] toutes les intersections de |D⃗| avec les ps. dr. passant par s'.
